arxiv-2204-04102.title: Huisken-Yau-type uniqueness for area-constrained Willmore spheres
arxiv-2204-04102.creator: Michael Eichmair, Thomas Koerber, Jan Metzger, Felix Schulze
arxiv-2204-04102.description: Abstract . Let ( M , g ) (M,g) be a Riemannian three-manifold that is asymptotic to Schwarzschild. We study the existence of large area-constrained Willmore spheres Σ ⊂ M \Sigma\subset M with non-negative Hawking mass and inner radius ρ \rho dominated by the area radius λ \lambda .

arxiv-2309-15908.title: QuCS: A Lecture Series on Quantum Computer Software and System
arxiv-2309-15908.creator: Zhiding Liang 1 Hanrui Wang 2
arxiv-2309-15908.description: Abstract In this era of incessant advancements in quantum computing, bridging the gap between quantum algorithms’ hardware requisites and available devices has become crucial. A prime focus in this context is the Software and System Level support for quantum computers, which has shown promising potential in significantly decreasing this gap.

arxiv-2402-05512.title: GPTs Are Multilingual Annotators for Sequence Generation Tasks
arxiv-2402-05512.creator: Juhwan Choi, Eunju Lee, Kyohoon Jin, Youngbin Kim
arxiv-2402-05512.description: Abstract Data annotation is an essential step for constructing new datasets. However, the conventional approach of data annotation through crowdsourcing is both time-consuming and expensive. In addition, the complexity of this process increases when dealing with low-resource languages owing to the difference in the language pool of crowdworkers.

arxiv-2408-03585.title: Hierarchical Neural Constructive Solver for Real-world TSP Scenarios
arxiv-2408-03585.creator: Yong Liang Goh, Zhiguang Cao, Yining Ma, Yanfei Dong, Mohammed Haroon Dupty, Wee Sun Lee
arxiv-2408-03585.description: Abstract . Existing neural constructive solvers for routing problems have predominantly employed transformer architectures, conceptualizing the route construction as a set-to-sequence learning task. However, their efficacy has primarily been demonstrated on entirely random problem instances that inadequately capture real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2408-15674.title: Boundary Bethe ansatz in massless
arxiv-2408-15674.creator: A
arxiv-2408-15674.description: Abstract We construct the boundary algebraic Bethe ansatz for the A ​ d ​ S 3 × S 3 × T 4 AdS_{3}\times S^{3}\times T^{4} integrable reflection problem restricted to the massless sector. We derive the double-row monodromy and find the appropriate formulation of the dual equation of Sklyanin’s.

arxiv-2505-14390.title: Comparison between Jacobi-Anger and saddle point methods to treat Above-threshold ionization
arxiv-2505-14390.creator: Danish Furekh Dar, Stephan Fritzsche
arxiv-2505-14390.description: Abstract We present a detailed comparison of theoretical approaches for modeling strong-field ionization by few-cycle laser pulses. The dipole approximation is shown to accurately capture interference structures in photoelectron spectra, while non-dipole effects introduce significant momentum shifts along the propagation direction.

arxiv-2506-14245.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs
arxiv-2506-14245.creator: Xumeng Wen, Zihan Liu, Shun Zheng, Zhijian Xu, Shengyu Ye, Zhirong Wu, Xiao Liang, Yang Wang, Junjie Li, Ziming Miao, Jiang Bian, Mao Yang
arxiv-2506-14245.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xumeng Wen, Zihan Liu, Shun Zheng, Zhijian Xu, Shengyu Ye, Zhirong Wu, Xiao Liang, Yang Wang, Junjie Li, Ziming Miao, Jiang Bian, Mao Yang. Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a promising paradigm for advancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs).

arxiv-2508-15828.title: Z-Pruner: Post-Training Pruning of Large Language Models for Efficiency without Retraining
arxiv-2508-15828.creator: Samiul Basir Bhuiyan 1 , Md. Sazzad Hossain Adib 1 , Mohammed Aman Bhuiyan 1 , Muhammad Rafsan Kabir 1 , Moshiur Farazi 2 , Shafin Rahman 1 , Nabeel Mohammed 1
arxiv-2508-15828.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly advanced in recent years, achieving remarkable performance across a wide range of natural language processing tasks. However, this progress has come at the cost of increasingly large model sizes, which pose significant challenges for deployment, scalability, and energy efficiency.

arxiv-2601-19512.title: Weak compactness in nice Musielak-Orlicz spaces Thanks: 1 Supported by NAWA under the Ulam postoctoral program 2024/1/00064 and partially supported by the research project 2025/00145/001 “Operadores, retículos y estructura de espacios de Banach”
arxiv-2601-19512.creator: Mauro Sanchiz 1
arxiv-2601-19512.description:
A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mauro Sanchiz 1. We prove two weak compactness criteria in Musielak-Orlicz spaces for N N -functions satisfying the Δ 2 \Delta_{2} -condition. They extend criteria from Andô for Orlicz spaces to this setting of non-symmetrical Banach function spaces. As consequences, we prove criteria for a sequence in a Musielak-Orlicz space to be weakly convergent, and show that Musielak-Orlicz spaces with the subsequence splitting property are weakly Banach-Saks. The study includes the case of Musielak-Orlicz sequence spaces. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
46E30

pmc-10547249.title: Pronation Reveals a Heterogeneous Response of Global and Regional Respiratory Mechanics in Patients With Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure
pmc-10547249.creator: Caio C.A. Morais, Glasiele Alcala, Roberta R. De Santis Santiago, Carlo Valsecchi, Eduardo Diaz, Hatus Wanderley, Bijan Safaee Fakhr, Raffaele Di Fenza, Stefano Gianni, Sara Foote, Marvin G. Chang, Edward A. Bittner, Ryan W. Carroll, Eduardo L.V. Costa, Marcelo B.P. Amato, Lorenzo Berra
pmc-10547249.description: OBJECTIVES:Experimental models suggest that prone position and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) homogenize ventral–dorsal ventilation distribution and regional respiratory compliance. However, this response still needs confirmation on humans. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the changes in global and regional respiratory mechanics in supine and prone positions over a range of PEEP levels in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients.

pmc-10721579.title: Associations of Awake Prone Positioning-Induced Changes in Physiology with Intubation: An International Prospective Observational Study in Patients with Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure Related to COVID-19
pmc-10721579.creator: Luis Morales-Quinteros, Raffaele Scala, João Manoel Silva, Antonio Leidi, Alexandre Leszek, Rodrigo Vazquez-Guillamet, Sergi Pascual, Ary Serpa-Neto, Antonio Artigas, Marcus J Schultz
pmc-10721579.description: IntroductionAwake prone positioning has the potential to improve oxygenation and decrease respiratory rate, potentially reducing the need for intubation in patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure. We investigated awake prone positioning-induced changes in oxygenation and respiratory rate, and the prognostic capacity for intubation in patients with COVID-19 pneumonia.

pmc-11336202.title: Simulating atmospheric drought: Silica gel packets dehumidify mesocosm microclimates
pmc-11336202.creator: S. Varghese, B. A. Aguirre, F. Isbell, A. J. Wright
pmc-11336202.description: As global temperatures rise, droughts are becoming more frequent and severe. To predict how drought might affect plant communities, ecologists have traditionally designed drought experiments with controlled watering regimes and rainout shelters. Both treatments have proven effective for simulating soil drought. However, neither are designed to directly modify atmospheric drought.

pmc-11360278.title: Unique Jurassic Ovaries Shed a New Light on the Nature of Carpels
pmc-11360278.creator: Qiang Fu, Jie Sun, Shaolin Zheng, Xin Wang
pmc-11360278.description: Enclosed ovules are a reproductive feature restricted to angiosperms. Although this feature can be used as a criterion for identifying fossil angiosperms, how ovules are enclosed and the nature of the placenta are still foci of debates. A reason underlying these controversies is the lack of reproductive organ fossils shedding light on these issues.

pmc-11516822.title: Health, an ageing labour force, and the economy: Does health moderate the relationship between population age-structure and economic growth?
pmc-11516822.creator: J Cylus
pmc-11516822.description: Research often suggests that population ageing will be detrimental for the economy due to increased labour market exits and lost productivity, however the role of population health and disability at older ages is not well established. Identifying whether the health of older people affects economic outcomes is challenging due to methodological issues.

pmc-11578372.title: ProT‐Diff: A Modularized and Efficient Strategy for De Novo Generation of Antimicrobial Peptide Sequences by Integrating Protein Language and Diffusion Models
pmc-11578372.creator: Xue‐Fei Wang, Jing‐Ya Tang, Jing Sun, Sonam Dorje, Tian‐Qi Sun, Bo Peng, Xu‐Wo Ji, Zhe Li, Xian‐En Zhang, Dian‐Bing Wang
pmc-11578372.description: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are a promising solution for treating antibiotic‐resistant pathogens. However, efficient generation of diverse AMPs without prior knowledge of peptide structures or sequence alignments remains a challenge. Here, ProT‐Diff is introduced, a modularized deep generative approach that combines a pretrained protein language model with a diffusion model for the de novo generation of AMPs sequences.

pmc-13187714.title: Strategic Decisions and the Entrepreneurial Mindset in Sustaining Agribusiness SMEs in Emerging Economies: Unlocking Pathways to Resilience – A Narrative Review
pmc-13187714.creator: Tom Ongesa Nyamboga, Monica Kagorora Kansiime, Asael Islas Moreno, Kingsley Kofi Arthur, Manoj P Samuel, Razia Muhammed, Kingsley Kofi Arthur
pmc-13187714.description: This narrative review examines how strategic decisions shaped by the entrepreneurial mindset sustain agribusiness SMEs in emerging economies, highlighting pathways to resilience. Recognising a critical knowledge gap in understanding the cognitive mechanisms that drive SME sustainability, the review is anchored in Entrepreneurial Cognition Theory and the Triple Bottom Line framework.

pmc-13563532.description: Post-mortem human brain tissue and in vivo imaging studies of behavioral variant frontotemporal degeneration (bvFTD) suggest that metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluR) may be vulnerable to the disease process. However, these studies lack evidence demonstrating how loss of mGluR relates to clinical features of bvFTD, hindering efforts to identify appropriate therapeutic strategies.
